fields.index_subject_description: 12-year-old male with VATER syndrome, bilateral cleft lip/palate and missing premaxilla
fields.chief_complaint: significant liquid passage into nose during eating and drinking with large oronasal fistula

evidence.quote: 12-year-old male

The patient was a 12-year-old male with a diagnosis of VATER syndrome and a complete bilateral cleft lip and palate. The patient had his premaxilla surgically removed by a previous surgeon during his primary lip repair. At presentation, the patient had a large oronasal fistula intraorally (Figures 1 and 2) due to his missing premaxilla with reports of significant liquid passage into his nose during eating and drinking. The patient was in mixed dentition, did not have any orthodontic preparation, had missing anterior teeth #7, 8, 9, and 10, and had a supernumerary tooth #56 adjacent to the defect. The patient was planned for surgical reconstruction with anterior iliac crest bone graft, extraction of supernumerary tooth #56, and oronasal fistula closure. The patient presented with bilateral posterior crossbite. This was not addressed preoperatively due to concerns that maxillary expansion would widen the cleft gap leading to larger and more difficult bone graft. After bone graft and skeletal maturity, the patient will be planned for maxillary advancement to address his maxillary hypoplasia and negative overjet.
The patient thereafter had an unremarkable hospital stay

The anterior iliac crest was selected due to low donor site morbidity, accessibility, and adequate bone volume for harvest. A 2 cm wide cortical block was harvested from the medial aspect of the left iliac crest using a reciprocating saw and osteotome. After harvesting the cortical block graft, cancellous bone was harvested from the iliac crest using bone curettes. After procurement of the graft, the site was irrigated, and the hip surgical site was then closed with appropriate multilayer closure.

evidence.quote: After bone graft and skeletal maturity, the patient will be planned for maxillary advancement to address his maxillary hypoplasia and negative overjet.

The patient was a 12-year-old male with a diagnosis of VATER syndrome and a complete bilateral cleft lip and palate. The patient had his premaxilla surgically removed by a previous surgeon during his primary lip repair. At presentation, the patient had a large oronasal fistula intraorally (Figures 1 and 2) due to his missing premaxilla with reports of significant liquid passage into his nose during eating and drinking. The patient was in mixed dentition, did not have any orthodontic preparation, had missing anterior teeth #7, 8, 9, and 10, and had a supernumerary tooth #56 adjacent to the defect. The patient was planned for surgical reconstruction with anterior iliac crest bone graft, extraction of supernumerary tooth #56, and oronasal fistula closure. The patient presented with bilateral posterior crossbite. This was not addressed preoperatively due to concerns that maxillary expansion would widen the cleft gap leading to larger and more difficult bone graft. After bone graft and skeletal maturity, the patient will be planned for maxillary advancement to address his maxillary hypoplasia and negative overjet.

The patient thereafter had an unremarkable hospital stay and was discharged on post-operative day 1. Post-operative instructions were given for 6 weeks of soft diet and 1 week of post-operative antibiotics with Augmentin. At 1 week and 3-months post-op, the patient had photographic and radiographic evaluation (Figures 4-6). At 13-month post-op, the patient had additional radiographs taken (Figure 7) all demonstrating stable bony fill after the operation. Final measurements of bone graft from Figure 7 at 13 months were 4.95 mm×13.05 mm at the most central portion of the graft.

summary.text: A 12-year-old boy with VATER syndrome and complete bilateral cleft lip/palate had undergone premaxilla removal during primary lip repair. He presented with a large oronasal fistula, liquid passage into his nose, missing anterior teeth, a supernumerary tooth, posterior crossbite, maxillary hypoplasia and negative overjet. No orthodontic preparation had occurred; preoperative expansion was deferred to avoid widening the defect.

Reconstruction used a 2 cm-wide nonvascularized left anterior iliac cortical block with cancellous bone, watertight nasal mucosal closure and locally applied rh-BMP2/collagen. No operative complication was reported. Supernumerary-tooth extraction was planned but not explicitly documented as completed.

He left hospital on postoperative day 1 with instructions for a 6-week soft diet and 1 week of Augmentin. One-week CT showed block placement; three-month imaging showed bony fill and bilateral class III malocclusion. Thirteen-month follow-up showed stable fill and fistula closure, with central graft dimensions 4.95×13.05mm. Future maxillary advancement remained planned after skeletal maturity, and dental-implant feasibility was uncertain.
